claim_one_line: THE DEDEKIND PHASE (sealed 20ed2c300; PROVED as sealed, a census informed by its own draft; the output committed unread at 5aea6a66c): on the ruled branch the triplet's two parameter-free Yukawa sectors -- the symmetric weight-1 coupling, which is the three theta constants placed off-diagonal, and the weight-0 Dirac coupling, which is the identity -- have m2/m1 >= 1/2 at every tau as the corollary of B1636's sum rule m1 = m2 + m3 (proved here symbolically: e1^2 = 4 e2 for the eigenvalues of Y Y-dagger, every complex a, b, c), with equality (1, 1/2, 1/2) at omega and (1, 1/phi, 1/phi^2) at i, and no Cabibbo angle (one form per sector, M_u proportional to M_d); so B1660's negative at omega is one point of a theorem. And the determinant of every T (x) T coupling is eta^6 times a level-one form (a constant at weight 1, E_6 at weight 3), so with CP-real coefficients theta-bar = pi Re(tau) + O(|q|): the strong CP angle is the Dedekind phase of the modulus, and theta-bar < 1e-10 puts tau on the CP-conserving axis where delta_CKM = 0; for R in Tbar the determinant is a level-one form (E_6 at weight 2), exponentially real toward the cusp, where the same limit degenerates the masses and kills J. The lowest fittable models (weight 3 for T (x) T, weight 2 for Tbar (x) T) miss the eight quark observables by chi^2 > 4e3 and 3e4. B1635's dimension table reproduced by piece. 0 of 19.
